text: A JWT carries claims in a signed token. The signature lets a server detect any change to the header or payload, but the payload itself is only encoded, not encrypted.
In Kafka, each partition of a topic is read by at most one consumer in a consumer group, so adding consumers beyond the number of partitions leaves some idle.
Redis can delete a key automatically after a time to live. Setting an expiry on cached values stops stale data from staying forever and limits memory use.
A multi-stage Docker build compiles the code in one stage and copies only the result into a small final image, so build tools do not end up in production.
A token bucket limits how often a client can call an API. Tokens refill at a steady rate, each request spends one, and a request with no token left is rejected.
A trace is a tree of spans. Each span records one operation with its start time and duration, and child spans show where time was spent inside a request.
A Kubernetes readiness probe tells the cluster when a pod can receive traffic. A pod that fails it stays running but is removed from the Service endpoints.
Terraform keeps a state file that records the resources it created. On the next plan it compares the state and the code to decide what to add, change or destroy.
gRPC defines services in protobuf files and sends binary messages over HTTP/2, which makes calls between internal services compact and strongly typed.
A WebSocket keeps one connection open after an HTTP handshake, so the server can push messages to the browser without the browser asking again.
